issues.legal_issue: The statutory category of persons eligible to receive donated land is limited by the purpose and scheme of the land-distribution movement, rather than the bare meaning of “landless persons.”
material_facts: The recipients obtained grants of land under the Act but were businessmen residing in the city, owned property there, paid income tax, and had their livelihood in trade rather than agriculture.
The recipients were not agriculturists and did not reside in the village where the granted land was situated.
The Additional Collector cancelled the grants; the High Court restored them on the ground that the recipients had no land in the village or district.
The grants were made before the 1975 amendment substituted “landless agricultural labourers” for “landless persons”.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the grants were inconsistent with the intended eligibility for Bhoodan land and restored the Additional Collector’s cancellation orders, setting aside the High Court’s judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14 and 15 of the U.P. Bhoodan Yagna Act, 1952 must be read together and interpreted in light of the Bhoodan Yagna scheme, the movement’s purpose, and the problem the Act was enacted to remedy. The scheme contemplated grants to landless agricultural labourers residing in the relevant villages, whose livelihood depended on agriculture and who had no land of their own. The 1975 amendment replacing “landless persons” with “landless agricultural labourers,” and its statement of objects and reasons, supported that interpretation. The Court also relied on purposive interpretation principles discussed in Lord Denning’s The Discipline of Law and on the description of the Bhoodan scheme in Vinoba and His Mission; it cited no earlier judicial case for this issue.

rule.if: bhoodan_land_grant_proceeding and (not recipient_is_agricultural_labourer or not recipient_lives_in_relevant_village or not recipient_depends_on_agriculture or not recipient_is_landless)

predicates.bhoodan_land_grant_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a grant of donated land made under a statutory land-distribution scheme.
predicates.recipient_is_agricultural_labourer: The recipient works as an agricultural labourer.
predicates.recipient_lives_in_relevant_village: The recipient resides in the village where the granted land is situated.
predicates.recipient_depends_on_agriculture: The recipient’s livelihood depends on agriculture.
predicates.recipient_is_landless: The recipient has no land of their own.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a grant under a donated-land scheme, the grant is liable to cancellation if the recipient is not an agricultural labourer, does not live in the relevant village, does not depend on agriculture, or is not landless.
